newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico looks for money laundering in food agency.
newsitem.headline: Mexico looks for money laundering in food agency.

text.p: Mexico's Attorney General Jorge Madrazo said on Monday he had launched an investigation into allegations of money laundering by the government's food distribution agency Conasupo.

He told a news conference the government had begun its own investigation after the Washington Post on Sunday reported that the United States Justice Department was looking into charges that the older brother of ex-President Carlos Salinas de Gortari used Conasupo to launder drug profits through U.S. banks.

Madrazo declined to give further information on the probe until his office decided whether there was sufficient evidence to charge anyone. Madrazo said U.S. authorities would be asked to share the information they have with their Mexican counterparts.

A leftist lawmaker Monday told reporters a congressional commission that last year investigated alleged corruption in Conasupo had found evidence of links between the food agency and the brother of a major druglord.
The commission was scrapped by the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), which has a congressional majority.

The congressman, Victor Quintana of the Party of the Democratic Revolution, said Daniel Garcia Abrego, brother of jailed drug kingpin Juan Garcia Abrego, had an account with Conasupo's milk arm, Liconsa.
He also sold grains to Conasupo in Tamaulipas, the hub of operations for his brother's Gulf Cartel, Quintana said.
"All this forms a series of indicators that, taken together, make sense and form a line of investigation that PRI deputies never wanted to pursue," he said.

The Post reported that the U.S. Justice Department probe was focused on whether Raul Salinas de Gortari used Conasupo to shield cocaine shipments into the United States and to launder drug money for the Gulf cartel through U.S. bank accounts and purchasing contracts.
The Post said the investigation began 18 months ago but had expanded rapidly in the past three months.

It quoted sources as saying that evidence was being collected that could implicate some of the most powerful people in the ruling PRI. Under investigation were party stalwart Carlos Hank Gonzalez and his son Jorge Hank Rhon.

DEA investigators were also looking into allegations that former president Salinas' chief of staff, Jose Cordoba Montoya, and private secretary, Justo Ceja Martinez, attended a key meeting with Raul Salinas, Mexico's secretary of the navy, and drug kingpin Garcia Abrego, according to the report.
Raul Salinas headed Conasupo during much of his brother's presidency. He is currently in jail near Mexico City on murder and illicit enrichment charges that he denies.
